task.title: Reduce cold filename traversal and warm-index filtering work
task.problem: Filename traversal without a warm index materializes every visited subdirectory as a BuildStream CasBasedDirectory object (_IndexEntry.get_directory caches it) and keeps it alive through the tree record, then stats each listed path from the root again. On freedesktop-sdk sdk.bst (468 trees, 598,531 files) a find without a warm index peaks at 1.64 GiB RSS with 35-39 s of traversal; a warm JSONL index needs 118 MiB and 7 s.
task.proposal: Walk Directory protos from the local CAS directly with an explicit stack, yielding regular files in the current order (sorted files, then sorted subdirectories) without retaining BuildStream objects or re-resolving paths; release each tree once traversed. Then profile warm-index filtering and evaluate safe directory pruning for narrow include prefixes. Never publish a query-filtered index as a complete tree index.
acceptance: Broad and narrow patterns preserve the same match set and order as the current implementation.
Peak RSS for find without a warm index stays within a small constant of the warm-index run on freedesktop-sdk sdk.bst.
Complete cached indexes remain valid across different later queries.
Report measured wall-time/RSS on fresh, warm and no index before changing the index format.
evidence: Dropping the tree's directory after traversal alone cut components/patch.bst peak RSS 318 -> 178 MiB locally; the rest is the largest single tree's cached objects.
